description: K2-Horizon-3.7B-4bit dense transformer with MIXED per-tensor quantization (qkv 8-bit/group-64, gate/up 4-bit/group-32), grouped RMSNorm (2 groups), nested rope_theta (1e7). Correctness and coherence MUST pass: engine-mlx is token-exact vs the reference k2_horizon.py (verified by the k2_horizon_token_parity gate), and chat prompts are rendered from the model's own chat_template.jinja (verified by serving_render_encode_matches_fixture). Served via the dense Qwen3 compiled forward.
notes: Dedicated profile for K2-Horizon, a *thinking* model (chat_template.jinja opens <ifm|think> with reasoning_effort=high and emits ~200 tokens of reasoning before the final answer). Tests use high max_tokens (1024/2048) so the final answer is not truncated by the preamble, and discriminators are preamble-tolerant (search the answer anywhere) without parsing the <ifm|think> channel. min_tps=5 is an honest pre-optimization floor: the measured throughput on a clean server is ~7.4-8.2 t/s on 256 tokens, so 5 leaves margin while still catching a real collapse. It is NOT a band-aid — the guard stays meaningful (15% default max_degradation_pct, no loose override). The sub-optimal throughput is tracked in ticket k2-horizon-support-01_37-decode-perf-optimization (target ~15-18 t/s after decode optimization); this profile will be recalibrated then. Correctness (factual/instruction) and coherence are HARD requirements — the engine is proven token-exact with k2_horizon.py at temperature 0 and renders the model's real chat template, so corrupted or degenerate output is a real regression, not a tolerance issue. This model requires mixed-quant support (per-weight group/bits) and a model that ships chat_template.jinja — a base model without one is not servable over /v1/chat/completions by design.
